name: AL-01

model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Carl's massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and market pricing near 96 percent all point the same way, leaving Jones needing an extraordinary shift to compete.
model.watch: A late scandal, a decisive national wave, or surprise polling showing a far closer race would be the main forces that could move this rating.

overview:
Alabama's first district is strongly Republican after redistricting, and the open-seat contest to fill it reflects that shape. Republican Jerry Carl has built a large financial advantage, raising more than $1.4 million with over half a million dollars in additional outside support, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised roughly $183,000 and enters the general election with limited resources.

No public general-election polling covers the race, so the outlook rests on the district's double-digit Republican lean, the fundraising gap, and betting markets that price Carl's chances near 96 percent. The national political environment offers Democrats some offset, but not nearly enough to close a structural deficit of this size. Absent an outside shock, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands.
